record.paper_title: Tiling by translates of a function: results and open problems
record.original_question: Let f be a nonzero function in L^1(R), and assume that the set of points x in R for which f(x) is not zero has finite Lebesgue measure. Let Lambda be a discrete subset of R with bounded density, meaning that sup over x in R of #(Lambda intersect [x, x+1)) is finite. Suppose that f tiles R at some level w with translation set Lambda, meaning that sum over lambda in Lambda of f(x-lambda) equals w for almost every x and the series converges absolutely almost everywhere. Must Lambda have periodic structure, meaning that Lambda can be represented as a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions a_j Z + b_j with real a_j > 0 and real b_j?

evidence.quote: We say that f tiles R at level w with the translation set Lambda, or that f + Lambda is a tiling of R at level w (where w is a constant), if we have sum over lambda in Lambda of f(x - lambda) = w a.e. and the series in (1.1) converges absolutely a.e.

Let f be a nonzero function in L1(R), and suppose that the set {x : f(x) != 0} has finite measure. If f tiles at some level w by a translation set Lambda subset R of bounded density, does it follows that Lambda has a periodic structure?

We say that a set Lambda subset R has a periodic structure if it can be represented as a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions, namely Lambda = union from j=1 to N of (a_j Z + b_j), where a_j, b_j are real numbers and a_j > 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f \in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ be a nonzero function, and assume that the set $\{x \in \mathbb{R} : f(x) \neq 0\}$ has finite Lebesgue measure. Let $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a discrete set of bounded density, meaning that 
$$\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} \#\bigl(\Lambda \cap [x, x+1)\bigr) < \infty.$$
Suppose that $f$ tiles $\mathbb{R}$ at some level $w \in \mathbb{R}$ by the translation set $\Lambda$, that is,
$$\sum_{\lambda \in \Lambda} f(x - \lambda) = w \quad \text{for almost every } x \in \mathbb{R},$$
with the series converging absolutely almost everywhere.

Say that a set $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}$ has a periodic structure if it can be written as a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions:
$$\Lambda = \bigsqcup_{j=1}^{N} (a_j \mathbb{Z} + b_j), \qquad a_j, b_j \in \mathbb{R},\ a_j > 0.$$

Must $\Lambda$ necessarily have a periodic structure?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the 2020 survey by Kolountzakis and Lev on tilings by translates of a function. Their earlier construction produces non-periodic tilings with f ∈ L^1(R) of bounded-density Λ, but f there does not have finite-measure support; the finite-measure-support case remains an open problem with no resolution found in subsequent literature (through 2025).

status_evidence.title: Tiling by translates of a function: results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on tilings by translates of an L^1 function, including the periodicity question for finite-measure support and bounded-density translation sets.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly posed as an open problem.
